findings.summary: CODEX-03-C meets all three acceptance criteria on the reviewed commit 12f81a9. It adds an invented-only continuation record that only a founder can create, with a three-step commit (database write, journal write, acknowledgement). A continuation period that is saved but not yet acknowledged is hidden from the family view (family-space projection) and also denied by the entitlement kernel's lockPeriod check. Expired periods reject new holds, while claims made before expiry and saved progress stay available. The family screen offers no purchase, renewal or payment-data collection. Controller evidence supports this: 90/90 tests, build, all ten protected probes plus the 76-case route/private-build checks, and an eight-scenario browser record bound to both origins and to source blobs matching this diff. Unresolved policy gates stay open (real payment arrangement, multi-host row locks, WM01/WM13 scheduler/alert, hosted restore and deletion), and nothing claims production readiness.

findings.title: No candidate typecheck evidence for the 'no introduced diagnostics' rule
findings.problem: The paid_continuation_instructions profile says to keep the 32 pre-existing whole-project type diagnostics disclosed and to fix any new ones. REPORT repeats the 32 baseline in its preparation section, but no tsc output was attached for this tree. check_application_card.py does not typecheck, Vite build does not typecheck, and the React test's transpileModule only reports syntax errors. So the evidence does not show that the LoopFamilyHome.tsx changes added no type errors. Reading the diff, they look type-safe (policy_version added to Allowance, unknown-typed catch), so this is an evidence gap, not a known defect.
findings.fix_check: Attach whole-project tsc output for the exact candidate commit, showing the diagnostic count is still 32 and none come from app/LoopFamilyHome.tsx or lib/loop/continuation-client.mjs.

findings.title: Committed contract doc and test headers still say 'not run/proposed'
findings.problem: The doc's Verification status section says all new tests, native checks and the existing '77 prototype tests' are NOT YET RUN. Its header says 'Not installed, executed, reviewed'. Both test files open with 'Proposed tests only'. The controller has since run 90 tests, the probes and the browser checks on this exact tree. The approved card requires recorded evidence to match the exact artifact. Stale wording in a shipped document could mislead later readers about what was verified, even though REPORT.md separates the two correctly.
findings.fix_check: Change the verification wording in the contract doc (and optionally the test headers) to say what was executed on the candidate commit and point to REPORT.md, or label the section explicitly as historical preparation text.

findings.title: Journal does not fsync its parent directory after first creating the file
findings.problem: The journal opens the file with O_CREAT and calls handle.sync() after each append, but it never fsyncs the directory after the file is first created. On some filesystems a crash could lose the directory entry. The contract already limits its durability claim to bounded single-host process recovery, and the hosted durability gate stays open, so this is a hardening note only.
findings.fix_check: Optionally fsync the directory after first creation, or record this in the contract's single-host limits.
